solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scoundrel put on British accent

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece put on another is placed after it

parts.note: a rogue is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A villain affects a British way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' places ROGUE after B.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a strong regional accent, especially an Irish or Scottish one.

clue.text: Queen's place is right behind revolutionary party

indicators.note: in a down clue, behind puts the right word below the reversed party
revolutionary means turning round, so the party name reads backwards

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
moral means right in the ethical sense

explanation.surface: The monarch's position supports a radical party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses the party; 'behind' puts the right word below it. Lab is the usual short name for Britain's Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral Castle is the British royal family's Scottish residence.

clue.text: Poem about many a mountain area is something refreshing

indicators.note: the poem word goes about, surrounding the other letters

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
a range is a line of many mountains

explanation.surface: Verse about a mountainous landscape proves invigorating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the poem round the other letters; 'many a mountain' is a whole chain of peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a sweet fruit drink, an example of a refreshment.

clue.text: Setter leaves CV around for operator

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the remainder reads backwards
leaves means the setter's word departs from the CV word

parts.note: a resumé is the same thing as a CV
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker quits around a job application for an operator post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes the setter to leave RESU, which 'around' turns about.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is one who operates something, as a computer user operates a machine.

clue.text: Dagger — it's flipping large in fight

indicators.note: in puts the reversed word and the large letter inside the word for a fight

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or brawl

indicators.note: flipping turns the word it over so it reads backwards

parts.note: the word it, with 's read as a link 'is'
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A knife is said to be swinging wildly about during a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns the pronoun round; 'in' sets it, with L, after the first letter of the fight word. A set-to is a brisk British word for a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short slender dagger, and gives its name to the thin-heeled shoe.

clue.text: Solicitor full of rage, with old penny spent

indicators.note: full of puts the other letters inside the solicitor word

parts.note: a tout solicits custom
ire is rage
d was the symbol for the pre-decimal British penny

explanation.surface: An angry lawyer has blown an old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a British lawyer but is one who solicits custom; 'full of' fills him with the anger and the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent and tired out both mean exhausted, with no energy left.

clue.text: They have property of drugs found by computer network

indicators.note: found by means the drugs are placed next to, and here below, the network

parts.note: LAN is a local area network
downers are depressant drugs

explanation.surface: Property owners whose wealth comes from narcotics discovered on a network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found by' sets DOWNERS beside LAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Landowners possess land, which is real estate.

clue.text: Monkeys, say, drink up, eating bagel

indicators.note: eating means the reversed drink swallows the ring letter
in a down clue, up means reading bottom to top

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
a bagel is ring-shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Apes finish their drink while chewing a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PORT into TROP, and 'eating' takes O in after TRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is the collective noun for a band of monkeys.

clue.text: Steer car in English city

parts.note: a steer is a castrated bull, an ox
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: An instruction to drive a vehicle within an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' reads as a verb about driving but is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford is an English university city; an oxford is also a shoe.

clue.text: Son taken in hand, partly, in bit of Bible

indicators.note: taken in means the son letter is held inside

parts.note: the palm is part of the hand

explanation.surface: A boy is led by the hand into a reading from scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' puts S inside PALM after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is one of the sacred songs of the Book of Psalms.

clue.text: The workshy having bananas for sale

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Idlers have fruit on offer at a market stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' rearranges FORSALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Loafers are idle people who avoid work; the word is also a slip-on shoe.

clue.text: Finish calling drummer thunderously

parts.note: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer
ff (fortissimo) is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A percussionist wraps up his playing with a loud crash.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring off is to end a telephone call by hanging up.

clue.text: Musical hero losing face in swinging event?

indicators.note: losing face drops the first letter, the front of the name

parts.note: Porgy is the title hero of Gershwin's Porgy and Bess

explanation.surface: A stage hero is humiliated at a lively party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing face' removes P from PORGY.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild party; 'swinging' hints at partner-swapping, hence the question mark.

clue.text: King leaving nobleman in helicopter is a churl

indicators.note: the shortened nobleman goes inside the helicopter word

parts.note: chopper is slang for a helicopter

indicators.note: the king letter leaves the word for a nobleman

parts.note: a lord is a nobleman
R (Rex) is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch steps out of an aircraft carrying a peer, and someone behaves boorishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes the king's letter out of the peer, and 'in' sets what remains after the aircraft's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a clumsy, boorish person, and also a heavy shoe.

clue.text: Duke's after week in the capital

indicators.note: after places the Duke below the week letter

parts.note: Duke Ellington was the jazz bandleader; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A duke's stay comes after a week spent in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke' suggests Wellington himself, but is Duke Ellington; 'after' sets him after W.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellington is the capital city of New Zealand.

clue.text: Come to a trail in water before noon

parts.note: a wake is the trail a boat leaves in water

explanation.surface: An invitation to visit a waterside path before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is to regain consciousness, which is to awaken.

clue.text: Roots go round furrow to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: to spin is to go round
a rut is a furrow

explanation.surface: Plant roots curl around a groove in soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the west' reverses SPINRUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnips are root vegetables, so they are examples of roots.

clue.text: Stages rap classes, welcoming learner

indicators.note: welcoming means letting the learner letter in

parts.note: a pat is a light rap
L is the learner-driver plate letter
forms are school classes

explanation.surface: Hip-hop lessons open to beginners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' puts L into PATFORMS after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: Platforms are raised stages, and platform shoes are a footwear style.

clue.text: Dread gathering round perhaps two or twelve answers here

indicators.note: gathering means the fear word collects the other letters inside it

parts.note: dread is fear
a round shape is like the letter O

indicators.note: perhaps signals the word two may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fear gathers round a couple of options among twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the number; 'gathering' puts it, after the round letter, inside the dread word. Twelve other answers in this grid are shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle's theme is shoes: brogues, loafers, mules and the like are all kinds of footwear.

clue.text: People creeping about, returning amid writhing snakes

indicators.note: amid places the reversed letters inside the jumbled ones
writhing means twisting, so the letters are jumbled
returning means the word for about reads backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Creepers slither about, coming back among twisting serpents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the word for about; 'writhing' reshapes the serpents as SNEAKS, and 'amid' sets the reversed pair before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneakers are people who sneak or creep; also American for trainers.

clue.text: Dickens admitting "I don't know line by current composer"

indicators.note: admitting means letting the other letters in

parts.note: Boz was Charles Dickens's pen name
er is a hesitant 'I don't know' sound
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A novelist confesses ignorance about a line by a living composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' lets the hesitation, the line and the current in between the pen name's B and OZ. Boz signed Dickens's early sketches.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector Berlioz was a nineteenth-century French composer, an example of the category.

clue.text: Decree from on high raid interrupts

indicators.note: interrupts means breaking into the middle of the other word
high suggests intoxicated, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: An order from above about a raid breaking in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' scrambles RAID to RDAI, which 'interrupts' ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to order or decree officially, as by authority.

clue.text: Witness watching the Ashes?

parts.note: at means attending, present at an event
the Ashes is a Test cricket series between England and Australia

explanation.surface: Seeing the England–Australia cricket contest in person.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the Test cricket series between England and Australia; the question mark flags a Test as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness to something, confirming it is true.

clue.text: Drug runners from Spain in northerly ghetto

indicators.note: in sets the Spain letter inside
in a down clue, going north means reading upwards

parts.note: a slum is a poor quarter like a ghetto
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Smugglers come from Spain into a run-down northern district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northerly' turns SLUM into MULS, with E inside before the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Mules are couriers who carry illegal drugs; a mule is also a backless shoe.

clue.text: Element of ice then dissolved in stomach

indicators.note: in puts the mixed letters inside the stomach word

parts.note: tum is an informal word for stomach

indicators.note: dissolved means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ice then melts in one's belly, chemically speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dissolved' rearranges the two words, and 'in' sets the result between the stomach's T and UM.
explanation.definitionFit: Technetium is a radioactive chemical element, number 43.

clue.text: Feature on American state in the east

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A news feature on a US state, set in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' suggests an article but is a part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: China is a nation in East Asia, and a state in the political sense.

clue.text: Ancient British king's erroneous answer

definitions.note: king's reads as 'king is', joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: off can mean wrong or mistaken

explanation.surface: An old monarch gives the wrong reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, famed for Offa's Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia in early medieval Britain.

clue.text: Cold lump of fig or lime, perhaps, in jam

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

parts.words: lump of fig or lime, perhaps
parts.note: fig and lime are trees, so a lump of their wood is a log

explanation.surface: A chilled piece of fruit sits in a preserve.
explanation.walkthrough: Fig and lime look like fruit in jam, but here they are trees giving wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To clog is to jam or block up; a clog is also a wooden shoe.

clue.text: Letter of English manor house across street

indicators.note: across means the house spans the street, placed around it

parts.note: pile is informal for a large stately house

explanation.surface: Correspondence from an English stately home on the other side of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' makes the house straddle the street. Pile is British slang for a grand country house.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, as in the New Testament epistles.

clue.text: Grow border of lobelia in green ground

indicators.note: in sets the border letters inside the mixed letters
ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up
the border of a word is its outside letters, first and last

explanation.surface: Lobelia planted along the edge of a lawn will spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border of' takes the flower's outside letters; 'ground' reshapes the colour as ENRGE, and 'in' plants the border after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge is to make or become bigger, so it means grow.

clue.text: Coaches or other vehicles that monarch boards

indicators.note: boards means gets on, so the monarch goes inside the vehicles

parts.note: trains are vehicles other than coaches
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Buses or rail carriages the Queen climbs aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coaches' looks like buses beside 'other vehicles', but is people who coach; 'boards' puts the monarch inside the vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainers are coaches who prepare athletes; the word is also a sports shoe.

clue.text: Expels, for example, powerless troublemakers

indicators.note: without power drops P, the symbol for power

parts.note: pests are troublemakers

explanation.surface: Weak agitators are thrown out, as one instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'powerless' removes P from PESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To egest is to discharge waste from the body, i.e. to expel it.
